headline: The studio taught itself to play Gauntlet
lede: Two commands, zero dependencies: record real games, clone the partner seat into a 1,517-number network, press M. On eight maze seeds it had never seen, the student won 8 of 8 — the same card the CPU teacher plays.

notes.text: PLAICRAFT pilot (#1625) shipped: export -> dataset -> BC trainer -> the trained net seated in Gauntlet slot 2 (M on hero select), plus a /research page with the numbers. Held-out seeds 100..107: model 8/8 wins, avg score 121,306 vs CPU 111,275 (+9%), 97.8% tick-level agreement; practice agreement matches held-out, so it generalises instead of memorising routes.

Every recording the pipeline made replays hash-exact against the sim (rec/v1, checkpoint every 30 ticks), and the new plaicraftcheck gate was mutant-proven: swap the brain for zeros and the agreement gate collapses 98.4% -> 74.5%. An earlier cut of the trainer did lie — a bias-index bug trained the net to 'always idle' at a suspiciously stable 73% accuracy; the mutant gate is what catches that class forever.

Slot b landed the WATCH key (#1634) the same night: MYST, Emberwood and SSX can now play themselves with their proven routes and hand back on any input. The warden's other half of the board closed too: #1570's ship record (prod-verify + labels) finished for the session that died at the merge.

Honest caveat, on the page and in the PR: the teacher is the studio's own CPU doctrine, not a human — chosen so 'model vs CPU on identical seeds' is exact. Cloning human recordings is the named follow-up.
